py37.label: Python 3.7 host tier (VFX Reference Platform CY2021 / CY2022 band)
py37.derivation: Per the per-host-year ruling, this tier is defined operationally: every component takes the HIGHEST release that still supports Python 3.7, read from PyPI requires_python metadata. That is what 'aligned to the host's year' means for a py37 host.
py37.derivation_probe: for each candidate version, admit it when Version('3.7.17') is in SpecifierSet(release.requires_python); take the maximum.

numpy.verified: numpy 1.21.6 is the last release whose requires_python admits 3.7; numpy 1.22 requires >=3.8.

pyside.verified: PySide6 6.5.3 is the last release whose requires_python admits 3.7.

pyside_essentials.verified: PySide6-Essentials 6.5.3 is the last release whose requires_python admits 3.7.

pyside2.verified: PySide2 5.15.2.1 is the last release whose requires_python admits 3.7.

pyqt.verified: PyQt6 6.6.0 is the last release publishing a cp37-abi3 wheel. 6.6.1 still declares requires_python>=3.6.1 but ships only cp38-abi3, and 6.7.0 raises the requirement to >=3.8, so the wheel tag is the binding constraint here rather than the metadata.

python37_floor.policy: The Python 3.7 floor is locked until the expiry date. Raising requires-python, narrowing the CI matrix, or deleting py37 wheels/jobs is forbidden before then.
